title: Chapter 138: It's Hiding Here
html:
“Wenlong? Pei Hu?” Xia Meili called their names twice, but not even an echo returned. It was as though a monster in the darkness had swallowed her voice.

What happened to them?She did not want to return to the cloyingly affectionate Wang Hailong and Dou Menglu, but exploring alone was worse. Could something have happened? Wenlong’s scream sounded angry, not endangered.

After hesitating among the doors, Xia Meili finally opened the nearest.

304? Why number the door? What does it mean?She peered inside and found a room far cleaner than expected.

Why does such a clean room make me uneasy?She called both names again, growing more anxious with each unanswered shout. Where could two grown men disappear to?

Her phone’s flashlight only deepened the surrounding shadows, and something seemed to move in the corridor behind her.

Standing out here is too dangerous. I should go inside.Xia Meili entered Room 304 and shut the door. It looks like an ordinary rental apartment, but that only makes it more suspicious. The owner wouldn’t build this set as decoration.

Cautious but braver than most, she kept her back to the wall and surveyed the apartment before taking one small step. After several minutes, she had found nothing unusual.

The living room is safe, so the danger must be in one of the other rooms. Wenlong and Pei Hu probably lowered their guard and triggered a trap.Clutching her phone, Xia Meili approached the bedroom.

There’s no door for an actor to hide behind, but the frame still creates blind spots. Be careful.Her heart beat faster as she advanced. At the threshold, she activated the camera, extended her phone inside, and swept it around.

She reviewed the dark recording. It was clear enough to confirm that no one hid inside.

No one? Wait—I haven’t checked beneath the bed.She retreated to the living room, crouched at a safe angle, and shone her flashlight underneath.

Nothing. I’ve watched too many horror movies.Xia Meili relaxed. If I designed the room, I wouldn’t waste the space under the bed. I’d rig a mannequin to spring out when someone sat down.

She entered the bedroom and found no traps at all, only a faint scent of detergent.

Even the cloth smells freshly washed. The tenant must be obsessed with cleanliness.Leaving the bedroom, Xia Meili faced the bathroom. Bathrooms are ideal for scares, but this one is tiny and has no cubicle. There’s nowhere for an actor to hide.

Xia Meili approached the Haunted House like a survival exercise, testing every step. Such visitors were a proprietor’s nightmare; they devised ways to expose each trap in advance and destroyed its impact.

Hai Ming Apartments’ bathroom layout was peculiar. The mirror faced the entrance, drawing the eye of anyone passing or entering. Xia Meili stared at her reflection and felt uneasy. Is it the atmosphere, or are my eyes playing tricks? Why does that reflection feel like someone else?

From the doorway, she aimed her phone at the glass. It reflects the beam, so it’s a real mirror—not an actor behind fake glass.

She held the wall as she entered the toilet. The space inside was small, and soon, she found herself standing before the mirror.

Either this room has no trap, or its actors left after frightening Wenlong and Pei Hu.Xia Meili touched the mirror, and her tension eased. It was only my imagination. Pei Hu’s cowardice infected me.

On closer inspection, her reflection looked normal. This is an ordinary Haunted House. We’ve been frightening ourselves. If Wenlong and Pei Hu aren’t here, they must be in another apartment.

Xia Meili called Wang Wenlong again. The ringtone is coming from next door.

She leaned sideways to listen. A drop of water fell from the ceiling and struck the sink, but her attention remained fixed on the ringtone. She never wondered why the ceiling was leaking.

It’s definitely coming from next door—Room 303.

Another drop landed on her shoe. Before she could react, a third struck her nose and ran down her face. At last she noticed. The Haunted House has a leak?

Frowning, she looked up. A drenched woman lay in the space above the ceiling, staring down with a face twisted in pain. Black hair spilled toward Xia Meili, its ends almost brushing her eyes.

No wonder I found nothing. It was hiding above me.

Something thicker than water splashed across her face. She wiped it away and found her fingers red with blood. Her strength vanished, and Xia Meili collapsed.

…

Chen Ge left the sealed classroom. Where is the mannequin I left here?

The girl had vanished. Remembering the black phone’s warning that spirits might go berserk outside their scenario, Chen Ge hurried toward the entrance.

The entrance boards remained undisturbed. He sighed with relief. Their time is almost up. I should bring them out.

Without even collecting his mallet, he entered wearing only the bloodstained costume. Halfway down the corridor, a woman’s piercing scream erupted from the girls’ dormitory.

That came from the Pen Spirit’s room, but she isn’t aggressive enough to provoke a scream like that.

He quickened his pace and soon saw a woman in shorts sprinting toward him, her heels gone.
